Vedic Routine

Guruvayur Temple Daily Pooja Timings & Darshan Schedule

The sanctum sanctorum opens at 3:00 AM for the auspicious Nirmalyam and follows continuous traditional rituals until closing at 9:15 PM.

Time (IST) Ritual / Pooja Ceremony Description & Devotee Instructions
03:00 AM Nirmalya Darshan Opening of sanctum sanctorum (Nada Thurakkal). View Lord Guruvayurappan adorned with previous day garlands.
03:20 AM - 03:30 AM Thailabhishekam & Vakacharthu Holy bath with medicated gingelly oil and cleansing Vakacharthu powder ritual.
03:30 AM - 04:15 AM Sankhabhishekam & Abhishekams Abhishekam with conch shell, sacred water, and milk.
04:15 AM - 04:30 AM Malar Nivedyam & Alankaram Offering of puffed rice, jaggery, plantains, and adorning the deity.
04:30 AM - 06:15 AM Ethruthu Pooja & General Darshan Morning pooja offering followed by general darshan for all devotees.
06:15 AM - 07:00 AM Morning Seeveli Sacred circumambulation with caparisoned elephant carrying the idol of the Lord.
07:15 AM - 09:00 AM Pantheeradi Nivedyam & Pooja Measurement-based offering of cooked rice and milk porridge.
11:30 AM - 12:30 PM Navakabhishekam & Ucha Pooja Noon pooja with sacred pots; main prasad offering (Paalpayasam).
01:30 PM Nada Adakkal (Afternoon Closing) Sanctum closes for the afternoon rest interval.
04:30 PM Nada Thurakkal (Evening Opening) Temple gates reopen for the auspicious evening session.
04:30 PM - 05:00 PM Evening Seeveli Elephant procession with ceremonial lamps around the inner prakaram.
06:00 PM - 06:45 PM Deeparadhana Grand illumination of hundreds of oil lamps across the Deepasthambham.
07:30 PM - 07:45 PM Athazha Pooja Nivedyam Night food offerings (Appam, Ada, Betel leaves) to the deity.
07:45 PM - 08:45 PM Athazha Pooja & Night Darshan Final regular darshan window before the night closing rites.
08:45 PM - 09:15 PM Thrippuka Burning of special herbal incense and natural camphor.
09:15 PM Harivarasanam / Nada Adakkal Sanctum closes with the chanting of the traditional lullaby.

Important Darshan Tips for Devotees:

  • Nirmalyam Darshan Queue: Devotees hoping to view Nirmalyam at 3:00 AM usually begin lining up outside East Nada by 1:30 AM to 2:00 AM.
  • Afternoon Break: The temple is closed between 1:30 PM and 4:30 PM. No darshan is conducted during this period.
  • Senior Citizens Line: Designated priority timings for senior citizens are typically arranged during specific morning and evening windows (verify at the Devaswom queue counter).
  • Deeparadhana (Lamp Illumination): Conducted at dusk around 6:00 PM – 6:30 PM, accompanied by the ringing of bells and the lighting of thousands of oil lamps.
